recursion.title: Recursion in Computer Science
recursion.summary: Recursion is a programming technique where a function calls itself directly or indirectly to solve a smaller instance of the same problem.
recursion.base_case: The base case prevents infinite recursion and stack overflow errors.
recursion.analogy: Imagine standing between two parallel mirrors; you see infinite reflections of yourself, each smaller than the last.
recursion.complexity: Time complexity typically ranges from O(N) for linear recursion to O(2^N) for naive branching recursion.

docker.title: Containerization with Docker
docker.summary: Docker packages applications and their dependencies into lightweight, isolated containers that run consistently across any computing environment.
docker.base_case: Images act as read-only blueprints, while containers are live, executable instances.
docker.analogy: Think of a shipping container: regardless of whether you put shoes, electronics, or coffee beans inside, any standard crane or cargo ship can handle it identically.
docker.complexity: Docker isolates processes via Linux kernel namespaces and cgroups, minimizing overhead compared to traditional VMs.

api.title: Application Programming Interfaces (APIs)
api.summary: An API is a standardized contract and communication protocol that allows different software applications to exchange data and invoke operations.
api.base_case: RESTful APIs typically use standard HTTP methods like GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE.
api.analogy: Like a waiter at a restaurant: you (the client) give your order to the waiter, the waiter takes it to the kitchen (server), and brings you back your meal (data).
api.complexity: Well-designed APIs follow idempotent patterns, structured JSON payloads, and clear status codes.

quantum.title: Quantum Computing Fundamentals
quantum.summary: Quantum computing leverages the principles of quantum mechanics—namely superposition and entanglement—to process complex information exponentially faster than classical computers for specific problem spaces.
quantum.base_case: Unlike classical bits (0 or 1), qubits can exist in a superposition of states |0⟩ and |1⟩ simultaneously.
quantum.analogy: A classical computer is like a mouse navigating a maze by trying one path at a time; a quantum computer is like water filling the entire maze all at once.
quantum.complexity: Quantum speedups are demonstrated by algorithms like Shor's (factoring in polynomial time) and Grover's (database search in O(sqrt(N))).

llm.title: Large Language Models & Transformers
llm.summary: Large Language Models are deep learning systems trained on massive text corpora using self-attention mechanisms to predict token probabilities.
llm.base_case: The Transformer architecture relies on Query, Key, and Value vectors to compute attention weights across context sequences.
llm.analogy: An incredibly well-read parrot with a photographic memory and an uncanny knack for knowing which word should statistically follow next.
llm.complexity: Self-attention has an O(N^2) complexity with respect to context length N, though modern flash-attention optimizes memory access.
